subject.title: [Bug]: auth-profiles test suite has cross-file mock/env leakage; directory run nondeterministically red

question: Should the protected-label auth-profile test isolation bug be promoted to an owner-handled fix now, and should the repair focus on shared OAuth mock helpers or individual leaking test files?
rationale: The protected `maintainer` label blocks automated cleanup/repair routing, and the current review did not run the expensive directory repro on current main.

options.title: Keep protected and owner-fix the suite
options.body: Have the auth-profile owner repair the mock/env/module cleanup and prove the full directory run on current main.

options.title: Clear protection for a repair lane
options.body: If maintainers decide this no longer needs protected handling, remove the protected signal and let a focused ClawSweeper repair job attempt the isolation fix.

options.title: Defer until a fresh repro is attached
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for a current-main Testbox transcript before prioritizing implementation.

recommendation.title: Keep protected and owner-fix the suite
recommendation.body: Have the auth-profile owner repair the mock/env/module cleanup and prove the full directory run on current main.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored the immediately related auth-profile fix and documented this exact test leakage as pre-existing and intentionally out of scope.
